judgedBy: single observer, one sitting. All forty portraits shot under identical lighting, lens and standoff-by-bounding-sphere. Azimuth chosen per asset by measured visible structure; elevation set per asset to the angle a standing player eye makes with it, clamped to +48/-55 degrees.

criteria.text: Does it read as the object it is named after, at a glance, at room distance? A clock needs a dial; a camera needs a lens. Failing this outranks every other defect because the player never gets to the second question.
Do the parts touch, sit and connect where physics would put them? Floating, detached or interpenetrating parts read as broken rather than as cheap.
Does the form carry structure beyond its primitive -- panels, reveals, mouldings, glazing bars, hardware -- or is it the bare box it started as?
Does the shading read as the material the object is supposed to be made of?
Are the proportions those of the real object?

note: Rank 1 is best. The ranking was fixed before any correlation was computed, and before the construction numbers for most of these assets had been looked at.

ranking.why: Glazed doors with muntins, internal shelves carrying trophies, lit valance, panelled base doors, cornice, plinth, brass ring pull. Deepest secondary structure in the set.
Banker's lamp: articulated arm with two real joints, shade, weighted base, emissive bulb. Instantly identifiable and elegantly proportioned.
Reads exactly as industrial racking -- upright frames, four shelves, a diagonal brace. Nothing is wasted and nothing is missing.
Correct object, legible lettering, twin lamp heads, sensible housing.
Cylinder, valve body, carry handle, hose, gauge and wall bracket all present and correctly related.
Grain visible on the worktop, dark legs, lower shelf, brass corner caps. Only asset in the set carrying an albedo map.
Five-star base with casters, gas stem, seat, back and headrest read immediately as an executive chair.
Pedestal desk with six drawers, pulls, plinth and an inset writing surface.
Overhead shelf on posts, drawer bank, worktop, backsplash. Composed like real back-of-house joinery.
Twin adjustable heads, housing, status LED. Correct and unfussy.
Plinth, capping rail, drawer bank and a reveal on the front panel, but a large bare field between them.
The radial strand fan genuinely reads as a mop head rather than a cone.
Board, ruled sheet, clip and pen. Simple, and every part is right.
Frame, cork field, pinned papers at varied angles.
Same family as the corkboard, slightly plainer frame.
Dividers, cards and a ring; reads as a rack, though the brass torus is unexplained.
Cylinder with two brass bands and a dark rim. Right silhouette, correct material read.
Handle, ferrule, block and bristle teeth. Reads correctly; the bristles are a row of prisms.
Drum, lid, hose, wand and floor nozzle. Correct, if soft in the details.
Clean box with a green cross and a handle. Correct but almost featureless.
Backboard, hooks and keys. Reads, but the board is a plain slab with one slot.
Hose loop, gun and lance with a coloured tip. Right object, minimal build.
Legs, apron and a lower shelf. Correct, generic.
Base, handset, keypad and cord present; entirely black and glossy, so the detail is hard to see.
Cushions and buttoning are there, but the shading reads as moulded plastic and the legs are token stubs.
A box with two trays and an LED. Identifiable only from context.
Box with a recessed door panel and a ring pull. Nothing wrong, nothing there.
Correct dome-camera silhouette -- dark dome on a cream base -- but completely featureless: no visible lens through the dome, no bezel, no housing seam. Placed on structure, not on identifiability.
Pan, lip and handle. Correct, and completely plain.
Two pale posts, a pleated curtain and a cap rail. Reads, but the posts are untouched boxes.
Bottle and trigger head are right; the label carries garbled pseudo-text and the nozzle is an unexplained brown ring.
Plate, dispenser and drip tray, with a floating green torus that corresponds to nothing.
Four drawers with recessed pulls on one face; every other face is a bare slab.
Soft, melted forms; the arm and back read as one lump and the legs are stubs.
A flat slab with one groove and an oval. No lettering, no pile, no edge.
Three rounded slabs. Does not read as cloth or as sponge.
Hose reel discs float clear of their axle, the pump reads as a gold treasure chest, and the wheels are half-buried in the base.
Three stacked rounded boxes with a twisted neck. Does not read as a bag at any distance.
Broken: the wringer handle floats detached above the bucket and the wringer body does not sit on the rim.
A blank domed disc with a single hand. No dial, no numerals, no bezel. Fails identifiability outright.

correction.reason: The first portrait pass shot every asset from a fixed +20 degree elevation. For an asset mounted above the player that photographs its ceiling plate, and asset_093 was ranked worst in the set on the strength of a view no player can ever have. tools/qa/proshop-asset-contact-sheet.js now derives elevation from the angle a standing eye makes with each asset, and from below the camera reads correctly as a dome camera. The re-rank is a correction to the instrument, not to the judgement: asset_087 was re-checked the same way and did not improve.
